label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**1 star — Good interface, but we need support when it matters**

Bridger Bend Community Library is a one-branch library with two full-time staff members, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Our catalog and circulation system went live on October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop, and our holds queue has been wiped out. We estimate that around 640 holds are gone. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We’ve received three replies, each saying the issue has been escalated to engineering.

These are not just numbers on a screen. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up large-print Westerns he had placed on hold. We had no record of his hold and had to send him home with nothing. Our volunteer has been writing checkouts on index cards like it’s 1975.

During the sales process, we were promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” Instead, we got a shared inbox. For a library our size, that difference matters when we can’t serve patrons normally.

I want to be fair: the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. My concern is not the product idea. It’s the support we’ve received when something went wrong.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I’m asking Stackhouse to have a named person call me this week, explain the status of the circulation and holds problems, and tell us what happens next.

I’m leaving one star for now. I’ll revisit this review if Stackhouse fixes the problems. In the meantime, I’d urge other library directors to get support response times in writing before signing.
